method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: NSAID gastrointestinal and renal toxicity: COX-2 selectivity, PPI co-prescription, renal monitoring
topic.coverageNote: Gastrointestinal risk reduction, COX-2 selection, and PPI co-prescription are explicit. Renal toxicity is named, but no monitoring interval is given, so none was invented.

mcqs.question: A patient who needs an NSAID has a prior ulcer. Which preventive strategy does the 2015 safe-prescribing consensus endorse?

options.A: Continue a full-dose non-selective NSAID with no gastroprotection
options.B: Use the lowest effective dose, add a gastroprotective drug, or choose a COX-2 selective agent
options.C: Substitute a high-dose COX-2 inhibitor specifically to protect the kidney
options.D: Rely on PPI therapy to prevent both upper- and lower-GI injury
options.E: Eradicate H. pylori and then stop all gastroprotection

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Use the lowest effective dose, add a gastroprotective drug, or choose a COX-2 selective agent
mcqs.explanation: The consensus states that patients at upper-GI risk should use the lowest effective NSAID dose, co-therapy with a gastroprotective drug, or a COX-2 selective agent.

sourceRefs.excerpt: patients at upper GI risk should have preventative strategies in place, including the use of the lowest effective dose of NSAID, co-therapy with a gastroprotective drug, or the use of a COX-2 selective agent

mcqs.question: According to that consensus, what is the limitation of a PPI when an NSAID injures the gut distal to the duodenum?

options.A: PPIs prevent NSAID damage throughout the small bowel
options.B: PPIs are unable to prevent NSAID-associated intestinal damage
options.D: PPIs replace the need for H. pylori testing in every NSAID user
options.E: PPIs are contraindicated with every COX-2 selective drug

mcqs.correctAnswerText: PPIs are unable to prevent NSAID-associated intestinal damage
mcqs.explanation: The consensus reports that PPIs do not prevent NSAID-associated intestinal damage, and that some COX-2 selective inhibitors showed better intestinal tolerability than non-selective NSAIDs with or without acid inhibition.

sourceRefs.excerpt: proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are unable to prevent NSAID-associated intestinal damage and that some COX-2 selective inhibitors display a better intestinal tolerability compared to traditional (i.e. non selective) NSAIDs, with or without acid inhibition

mcqs.question: Which organs does the consensus list among sites of NSAID adverse reactions?

options.B: Liver, kidney, cardiovascular system, skin, and gut
options.E: The consensus states NSAIDs have no organ toxicity

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Liver, kidney, cardiovascular system, skin, and gut
mcqs.explanation: The text says NSAID use is associated with adverse reactions involving the liver, kidney, cardiovascular system, skin, and gut, with GI effects the most common.

sourceRefs.excerpt: their use is associated with a broad spectrum of adverse reactions involving the liver, kidney, CV system, skin, and

mcqs.question: A prescribing audit cited in the consensus found which pattern of PPI co-prescription?

options.A: High rates of PPI co-prescription with non-selective NSAIDs in patients with increased GI risk
options.B: PPIs were never co-prescribed with NSAIDs
options.C: PPIs were reserved only for COX-2 selective drugs
options.D: Every low-GI-risk patient was left without a PPI, matching guidance exactly
options.E: PPI use was limited to people with a history of H. pylori

mcqs.correctAnswerText: High rates of PPI co-prescription with non-selective NSAIDs in patients with increased GI risk
mcqs.explanation: The cited audit showed high rates of PPI co-prescription with non-selective NSAIDs when GI risk was increased, while also describing inappropriate use in some lower-risk patients.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The study showed high rates of PPI co-prescription with ns-NSAIDs in patients with increased GI risk.

mcqs.question: What does this consensus provide about a schedule for renal-function monitoring during NSAID use?

options.A: Check creatinine weekly for the first month
options.B: It lists the kidney as a toxicity site but does not set a monitoring interval
options.C: Stop NSAIDs if eGFR falls by 1%
options.D: COX-2 selective drugs require no renal consideration
options.E: Renal monitoring is required only after a PPI is added

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It lists the kidney as a toxicity site but does not set a monitoring interval
mcqs.explanation: Kidney injury is named among NSAID adverse reactions, but the consensus text used here does not specify a creatinine or eGFR monitoring schedule.

sourceRefs.excerpt: adverse reactions involving the liver, kidney, CV system, skin, and gut
